feedback: Anne's confession follows the strongest pre-vote contradiction: the tour never accompanied her to the glass. It confirms the inferred transfer rather than supplying a new forensic exclusion, so I would not call its new wording a decisive missing clue. The borrowed-group admission makes emotional sense, and the final reference to children hearing why her name has disappeared is affecting. Elle and Monet admitting their financial misconduct gives their earlier denials credible alternate meanings. My remaining reservation is comparative certainty: those financial admissions do much of the work of closing competing cases after voting. The finale feels earned as an answer to Anne's arc, while the available evidence supported a best bet more strongly than a uniquely compelled proof.
